name: Phillips 66
reason: Refining-led earnings swing with crack spreads (EPS -0.89 in 2020 to 18.79 in 2022, now 0.34x 10y peak) so cannot be forecast; commodity margin business with no specialness.

name: Chemours Co.
reason: TiO2/fluoro commodity chemicals with PFAS litigation overhang, EPS 0.17x 10y peak and net debt/EBITDA 5.7x.

name: HubSpot, Inc.
reason: Strong 33% revenue CAGR but GAAP EBIT margin only 0.4% (adj-vs-GAAP gap huge from SBC) and SMB CRM/marketing software faces credible AI disintermediation within 5 years.

name: Enova International, Inc.
reason: Non-prime online consumer/SMB lender whose earnings depend on the credit cycle, EPS at 10y peak with net debt/EBITDA 5.3x.

name: Byline Bancorp, Inc.
reason: Ordinary Chicago commercial/CRE bank with share count up 10%/yr from acquisitions and no evident deposit-franchise or underwriting edge; EPS at 10y peak after rate tailwind.

name: Par Pacific Holdings Inc
reason: Small refiner with crack-spread-driven earnings (EPS 0.37 in 2024 vs 7.56 in 2025, 0.92x 10y peak) and acquisitions exceeding FCF (acq/FCF 1.22).

name: National Bank Holdings Corporation
reason: Plain-vanilla regional bank with EPS flat for 5 years (1.0% CAGR) and ROE ~8.7%; cheap but not special.

name: RH
reason: Luxury furniture tied to the housing cycle, EPS 0.24x 2021 peak with net debt/EBITDA 7.3x after debt-funded buybacks (buyback/FCF 2.05).

name: BILL Holdings, Inc.
reason: SMB AP/payments software only just GAAP-breakeven (EBIT margin 1.1%), revenue partly float/interest-driven and facing fintech/ERP and AI competition; long-run economics hard to forecast.

name: Collegium Pharmaceutical, Inc.
reason: Opioid/pain portfolio built by acquisition (acq/FCF 1.09) with patent/LOE cliffs and opioid litigation/regulatory risk inside 5 years; 3x P/E reflects that.

name: Organon & Co.
reason: Off-patent established-brands pharma with GAAP EPS falling from 12.71 (2019) to 0.72, net debt/EBITDA 5.0x and ongoing LOE erosion.

name: Energizer Holdings, Inc.
reason: Mature battery/auto-care brands with 2.2% 10y EPS CAGR, acquisition-funded (acq/FCF 1.73) and net debt/EBITDA 5.05x; no growth route to 7%.

name: PayPal Holdings, Inc.
reason: Cheap (9.9x) with 15% 10y EPS CAGR, but branded checkout is losing share to Apple Pay/wallets and EBIT margin is at its 10y high (19.7%), so 5-10y share and take-rate are hard to forecast.

name: TransUnion
reason: One of three US credit bureaus (true oligopoly) with 14.7% 10y adj EPS CAGR and 12-15% consensus growth; watch acquisition-heavy history (acq/FCF 1.62), ND/EBITDA 2.9x and large adj-vs-GAAP gap from deal amortization.

name: Kraft Heinz Company
reason: Shrinking packaged-food brands with 1.7% 10y EPS CAGR, ROIC ~1% after impairments and consensus EPS decline; GLP-1 and private-label pressure.

name: Sunrun Inc
reason: Residential solar dependent on tax-credit policy and capital markets, persistent GAAP operating losses and net debt/EBITDA 19.6x.

name: Planet Fitness, Inc.
reason: Asset-light HVLP gym franchisor with a clear low-price value proposition, 19% 10y EPS CAGR (9/10 years of 7%+ growth) and 12-15% consensus; securitized leverage 4.4x net debt/EBITDA is the key watch item.

name: Zillow Group, Inc.
reason: Housing-transaction-dependent portal still GAAP loss-making (EBIT margin -1.2%) with listing-access litigation and agent-commission rule changes making 5-10y economics unforecastable.

name: Ingevity Corporation
reason: Pine-chemicals business classified as commodity chemicals with restructuring, flat 1.9% 10y revenue CAGR, ROIC 4.8% and auto carbon-canister franchise exposed to EV adoption.

name: GigaCloud Technology, Inc.
reason: Fast-growing B2B large-parcel marketplace (GAAP EPS 0.03 to 3.59 since 2019) but short public history, China-linked supply chain and tariff exposure make durability impossible to judge.
